subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be resolved from live gateway runtime health, from a passive local plugin status contract, or should current `not checked` output be considered sufficient for this issue?
rationale: Current main only mitigates the old wording, while the requested behavior, the broader open issue, and the conflicting fork PR require an owner decision about the permanent status boundary.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove human and JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept current mitigation
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for normal/deep status, close the conflicting fork PR, and document that detailed memory health belongs to all-mode or memory-specific commands.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent changes in the shared memory status snapshot make this the closest current implementation owner for the status contract decision.
